title: Privacy-provisioned-permission-aware RAG in cloud using identity and access management, trust and large-language models (PPPARITL)
research_question: Can a cloud-based RAG architecture combine identity and access management, dynamic trust assessment, encrypted embeddings, and malicious-query controls to reduce unauthorized information access while retaining useful LLM-assisted retrieval?
methodology: The paper proposes PPPARITL, a two-stage permission-aware RAG architecture in which an IAM-controlled Role-Resource-Action-Condition gate first filters access according to administrator-defined ACL rules. Document and query embeddings are protected at rest with CKKS homomorphic encryption, and only authorized candidates are decrypted before similarity ranking; a subsequent trust score uses contextual, behavioral, and historical user interactions to govern permission-aware retrieval. A sanitization and monitoring layer detects malicious query patterns and supports revocation. The accessible abstract reports simulation experiments against baseline access-control approaches on a synthetic enterprise dataset.

key_findings.finding: PPPARITL places authorization filtering before similarity ranking, so only candidates passing the RRAC access-control gate are eligible for decryption and retrieval.
The framework combines static IAM policy enforcement with a second-stage trust score derived from contextual, behavioral, and historical interactions.
Document and query embeddings are protected at rest using CKKS homomorphic encryption, with the decryption key held by an administrator.
The architecture includes query sanitization and continuous malicious-query monitoring intended to mitigate denial-of-service and insider threats and to support user revocation.
On the reported synthetic enterprise evaluation, the proposed approach reaches 95.84% authorization accuracy and reduces the False Access Rate relative to baseline access-control approaches.

limitations: Only the abstract and publisher metadata were accessible through the available web interface, so implementation details, baseline definitions, statistical analysis, and ablations could not be independently inspected.

The reported experiment uses a synthetic enterprise dataset, leaving performance on real organizational identities, policies, documents, and adversarial workloads unestablished in the accessible text.
The accessible abstract does not report retrieval-quality or answer-quality metrics alongside authorization metrics.
The accessible text does not evaluate temporal validity, document-version provenance, explicit evidence-gap tracking, or calibrated retrieval stopping.
The architecture relies on an administrator-held secret key for candidate decryption, creating a centralized trust dependency that is not evaluated in the accessible abstract.
raw_claims: The proposed system adds privacy and permission controls to a RAG pipeline used in a cloud setting.
An RRAC policy gate checks each request against administrator-configured access-control rules.
Only candidates that pass authorization are decrypted for similarity ranking.
CKKS encryption is used to protect document and query embeddings at rest.
A trust score incorporates contextual, behavioral, and historical information about service-user interactions.
The trust score influences permission-aware retrieval after the initial access-control gate.
A sanitization layer is intended to reject malicious query patterns and mitigate denial-of-service behavior.
The system continuously monitors requests and can revoke users when malicious behavior is detected.
The reported synthetic-enterprise experiment reaches 95.84% authorization accuracy.
The paper reports a reduction in False Access Rate compared with its baseline access-control approaches.
